statement: A railway station serves n trains in one day. Train i arrives at time arrival[i] and departs at time departure[i]; times are written as numbers such as 900 for 9:00.

A train occupies a platform from its arrival to its departure, inclusive. A platform cannot be used for one train's departure and another train's arrival at the same moment, so two trains whose times touch need different platforms.

Return the minimum number of platforms needed so that no train has to wait. Sort the arrival times and the departure times separately and sweep through both in time order: an arrival takes a platform and a departure frees one. The most platforms in use at once is the answer.

examples.explanation: Between 11:00 and 11:20 the trains that arrived at 9:40, 9:50 and 11:00 are all at the station, so 3 platforms are needed. No moment has more than three.
Each train leaves before the next arrives, so one platform serves them all.
The second train arrives at 200, the same moment the first departs. That counts as an overlap, so two platforms are needed.
